findings.passage: Secretary of State Jocelyn Benson has even conceded that their ballots were counted and impacted the results of our elections. This is unconscionable and proof that we need voter ID requirements. Michigan’s elections should be decided by the citizens of Michigan alone.
findings.note: Statement given to WHMI when he announced a bill requiring proof of citizenship to register. He ties it to non-citizen voting and calls for voter ID requirements.

findings.passage: "Michigan families are tired of wondering if their vote will still count," Rep. Woolford told the House Election Integrity Committee.  "We've seen documented instances where non-citizens ended up on the voter file, not only here in Michigan, but around the United States.  So it's important we remember every improper ballot cancels out the lawful vote of a Michigan citizen."
findings.note: Remarks to the House Election Integrity Committee on House Bill 4765 (proof of citizenship to register), as reported by WHMI.

findings.passage: This is not a partisan issue.  In fact, polls show over 80 percent of Americans, including a large majority of Democrats and independents, support requiring proof of citizenship to vote.
findings.note: Committee remarks, as quoted by WHMI. He says broad public support exists for proof of citizenship.

findings.passage: Let us pass House Bill 4765 and send a clear message to our citizens that voting matters. Citizenship matters. That the rule of law matters and that the voice of every lawful vote in this state will be protected,
findings.note: Speech in the Election Integrity Committee supporting HB 4765, which requires photo ID plus proof of citizenship to register and vote (WWMT report).

findings.passage: “There needs to be, in our voting, no chaos, no games, and no dilution of citizens and their votes.”
findings.note: Committee remarks on HB 4765 as quoted by WNEM.

findings.passage: “Michiganders deserve to have their voices respected,” Woolford said. “Unfortunately, without requiring identification, we have been threatening the sanctity of our voting process. The people of Michigan deserve better, and today we delivered. We need to do everything in our power to ensure that our elections are free from foreign interference. An identification requirement should be the bare minimum.”
findings.note: Statement after the House passed HB 4765, as published by WHMI.

findings.note: He introduced House Bill 4586 of 2025, which amends section 5b of 1927 PA 372 to change the age requirement for a concealed pistol license (the bill is described elsewhere as lowering it from 21 to 18). The page lists Ron Robinson and Matt Maddock as co-sponsors.

findings.passage: "At 18 years old, you are legally recognized as an adult," said Woolford. "You can vote, serve on a jury, sign contracts, and enlist in the military."
findings.note: As quoted by WHMI on HB 4586, he says an 18-year-old has the legal rights of an adult.

findings.passage: "If an 18-year-old is trusted to carry a firearm in defense of our nation, they should also be trusted to carry a sidearm for their own self-defense here at home."
findings.note: As quoted by WHMI, he argues that young adults trusted with a firearm in the military should be able to carry a sidearm at home for self-defense.

findings.passage: "HB 4586 is about ensuring that all legal adults are treated equally under the law and trusted to exercise their constitutional rights responsibly."
findings.note: As quoted by WHMI, he describes HB 4586 as equal treatment of legal adults in exercising constitutional rights.

findings.passage: “It’s a constitutional right and we’ve got to fix this contradiction,” he told News 10. “We let 18-year-olds openly carry a handgun, but they say they’re too immature to put on a coat and carry a concealed until they’re 21 years old.”
findings.note: Quoted by WNEM (TV5/News 10 reporting) on why the concealed pistol license age should be 18.

findings.passage: "Every safeguard that exists in our current concealed carry process remains fully intact," Woolford said.
findings.note: Quoted on a gun-rights site about HB 4586: the bill keeps the other concealed carry requirements and changes only the age.

findings.passage: At the time, I was firing M60s, rocket launchers, and 9mm handguns. But back home, I would not be allowed to buy a pistol.
findings.note: Quoted on a gun-rights site: he cites his Marine service at 19 against the age limit for buying a pistol.
